title: Grüezi
desc: One word, and everybody uses it
german: Grüezi, Grüezi mitenand, merci, danke; sein in the present
swiss: You land at Zurich Kloten, not Luzern; Grüezi is said to strangers, and not saying it is noticed
beat: You say nothing to anyone for forty minutes and feel it.

title: Gleis sieben
desc: Numbers, and a platform you have to find
german: numbers 1-20; wo ist; der/die/das on things you can point at
swiss: The train leaves from under the airport; Swiss trains go when they say they go
beat: You find the platform with ninety seconds to spare.

title: Der Zug nach Luzern
desc: An hour of a country going past
german: der Zug, die Fahrt, das Fenster; fahren, sehen, sein in the present
swiss: Zurich to Luzern is about an hour, and nobody talks on the train
beat: You watch a lake, a tunnel, another lake, and then it stops.

title: Angekommen
desc: A station with an old gate standing in front of it
german: ankommen, aussteigen; hier, dort, da; plain statements
swiss: The stone portal outside Luzern station is all that survived the fire of 1971
beat: You stand under an arch that leads nowhere and put your bag down.

title: Ein Kaffee, bitte
desc: The first thing you order on purpose
german: ich möchte, ich hätte gern, bitte, danke; ein/eine
swiss: Coffee is ordered small and drunk sitting down; merci is ordinary German here
beat: Lea corrects your order without making it a lesson.

title: Gipfeli
desc: Bread has different names here
german: das Brot, das Gipfeli, das Weggli; kaufen, nehmen, kosten
swiss: Gipfeli not Croissant, Weggli not Brötchen; a Swiss bakery opens early and sells out
beat: You point at something and get something better.

title: Franken und Rappen
desc: Money that is not yours yet
german: numbers to 100; kosten, bezahlen; wie viel
swiss: The franc, the Rappen, prices ending in .95, and cash that still works everywhere
beat: You hand over fifty francs for a coffee and get a look.

title: Migros oder Coop
desc: Two shops, and there are only two
german: food nouns and their genders; brauchen, suchen, finden
swiss: Migros and Coop are the whole country; Migros has never sold alcohol
beat: You go to Migros for wine and come out with chocolate.

title: Das Wasser ist gratis
desc: You can drink from the fountains
german: trinken, das Wasser, gratis; kann ich
swiss: Luzern's public fountains run drinking water; buying it in a bottle marks you out
beat: Somebody watches you buy a bottle and tells you, kindly.

title: Wo ist die Post?
desc: Asking, and understanding half the answer
german: wo ist; links, rechts, geradeaus; die Strasse, der Platz
swiss: The Swiss will walk you there rather than explain it; the post office is yellow
beat: You ask for directions and get an escort.

title: Der See
desc: Water with mountains standing behind it
german: der See, der Berg, das Schiff; gross, schön, kalt
swiss: The Vierwaldstättersee, and why one lake carries four names
beat: You see it for the first time and stop walking.

title: Die Kapellbrücke
desc: A wooden bridge with paintings in the roof
german: alt, neu, über; gehen, stehen, schauen
swiss: The Kapellbrücke burned in 1993 and was rebuilt; the Wasserturm is older than the bridge
beat: You cross it four times because there is nowhere else you need to be.

title: Punkt acht
desc: Time, said exactly
german: telling the time; um, halb, viertel; früh, spät
swiss: Swiss punctuality is not a stereotype, it is a timetable everybody actually keeps
beat: You arrive four minutes late and are the only one who does.

title: Am Sonntag ist zu
desc: The day everything stops
german: days of the week; offen, geschlossen, zu; öffnen, schliessen
swiss: Sunday closing is close to total, and the station shops are the exception everybody knows
beat: You run out of milk on a Saturday night and learn something.

title: Es regnet
desc: Weather you will talk about every day
german: es regnet, es schneit; kalt, warm; das Wetter
swiss: Luzern rains more than Zurich and everybody says so; the Föhn, and what gets blamed on it
beat: Three people tell you about the weather before ten in the morning.

title: Die erste Nacht
desc: A room, a window, and a great deal of quiet
german: review of the present tense, der/die/das, numbers; müde, allein
swiss: How quiet a Swiss town goes after ten, and how loud that quiet is
beat: You lie awake listening to nothing at all.

title: Die Wohnung
desc: Somewhere to put your things
german: die Wohnung, das Zimmer, der Schlüssel; accusative on objects
swiss: Flats are handed over spotless and taken back spotless; the Wohnungsabgabe is inspected
beat: You are given three keys and told what each one is for, twice.

title: Frau Amrein
desc: The door across the landing opens
german: introductions; wohnen, heissen, kommen; Sie as the default
swiss: Neighbours greet, and a neighbour who does not greet you is making a point
beat: She has your name before you have hers.

title: Die Hausordnung
desc: Rules on a laminated sheet
german: modal verbs: müssen, dürfen, können; man darf nicht
swiss: Every Swiss building has a Hausordnung and it is not decorative
beat: You read it twice and understand about half.

title: Die Waschküche
desc: A laundry room with a list on the wall
german: waschen, trocknen, eintragen; word order with modals
swiss: The Waschküche rota is the most serious document in the building
beat: You wash on somebody else's day and hear about it.

title: Der Hauswart
desc: The man who keeps the building
german: reporting a problem; kaputt, funktioniert nicht; separable melden
swiss: The Hauswart is not a landlord and not a servant, and knowing the difference matters
beat: Ruedi Zemp looks at your bicycle for a long moment and says nothing.

title: PET, Alu, Karton
desc: Rubbish, sorted four ways
german: das Glas, das Papier, der Karton; wohin kommt; trennen, sammeln
swiss: Glass goes by colour, PET to the shop, cardboard bundled and tied on its day
beat: You put cardboard out on the wrong morning and it is still there at six.

title: Der Gebührensack
desc: You have to buy the bag
german: der Sack, die Gebühr; kaufen, bezahlen, wegwerfen
swiss: Rubbish is taxed by the bag; the wrong bag is not collected and gets opened
beat: Your bag is left behind with a sticker on it.

title: Ruhezeiten
desc: The hours when you make no noise
german: die Ruhe, laut, leise; nach zehn, am Mittag; darf man nicht
swiss: Quiet from ten at night, quiet at midday, and no drilling on Sunday
beat: You run a washing machine at eleven and the ceiling knocks.

title: Die Anmeldung
desc: Fourteen days to tell them you exist
german: das Formular, der Ausweis, ausfüllen, unterschreiben
swiss: You register with the Gemeinde within two weeks and everything else follows from it
beat: You take a number and wait, and it takes eleven minutes.

title: Die Krankenkasse
desc: Insurance you have to choose
german: die Versicherung, die Prämie; vergleichen, wählen, bezahlen
swiss: Health insurance is compulsory, private, and yours to pick within three months
beat: You compare eleven of them and pick the one Nuno has.

title: Ein Brief von der Serafe
desc: A bill for a television you do not own
german: der Brief, die Rechnung; bekommen, öffnen, verstehen
swiss: The broadcasting levy is charged per household, television or no television
beat: You read it four times looking for the mistake.

title: Die Post
desc: Yellow, and everywhere
german: das Paket, die Briefmarke, schicken, abholen
swiss: The Post does banking, and the yellow is a national colour
beat: You queue behind a man paying his bills in cash.

title: Das Brockenhaus
desc: A whole flat, secondhand
german: die Möbel, der Tisch, der Stuhl, billig, teuer
swiss: Brockenhäuser are charity warehouses and furnishing from one is normal, not poor
beat: You buy a table that is better than anything you would have bought new.

title: Der Nachbar unten
desc: Somebody lives below you
german: der Nachbar, der Boden, die Decke; stören, hören
swiss: Complaints go to your door before they go to the Hauswart, and that is the polite order
beat: He is at your door before you have taken your shoes off.

title: Nuno
desc: The first person who is not being polite at you
german: talking about work; arbeiten, seit, schon; simple past questions
swiss: A quarter of Switzerland was born somewhere else, and Luzern is no exception
beat: He tells you he has been here eighteen years and still says the articles wrong.

title: In der Apotheke
desc: Being ill in a language you do not have
german: der Kopf, der Hals, weh tun; ich brauche etwas gegen
swiss: Pharmacists here diagnose and advise, and you go to them before a doctor
beat: You point at your throat and get exactly the right thing.

title: Das Konto
desc: A bank that wants to know everything
german: das Konto, die Karte, die Nummer; eröffnen, brauchen
swiss: You need an address to open an account and an account to get an address
beat: You bring four documents and are asked for a fifth.

title: Ein Abo
desc: A phone number of your own
german: das Handy, die Nummer, der Vertrag; monatlich, kündigen
swiss: Everything here is an Abo, and every Abo has a notice period
beat: You sign for two years without meaning to.

title: Die Rechnung
desc: A bill with a square on it
german: überweisen, einzahlen, der Betrag, das Datum
swiss: Bills arrive on paper with a QR code and are paid by transfer, not by card
beat: You pay it standing at the counter because you do not trust the app yet.

title: Fasnacht
desc: The city detonates and nobody warned you
german: die Musik, die Maske, laut; questions under pressure
swiss: Luzerner Fasnacht starts before dawn on Schmutziger Donnerstag and runs to Aschermittwoch
beat: You wake at five to brass instruments deliberately playing wrong.

title: Falsch getrennt
desc: Your rubbish is corrected
german: das gehört nicht dahin; correction and mild reproach; accusative practice
swiss: Being told off about recycling is a form of being taken seriously
beat: Frau Amrein shows you what you did and then gives you soup.

title: Ein Monat
desc: The flat stops being a place you are staying
german: review of modals and accusative; sich gewöhnen an
swiss: How long a Swiss winter evening is, and what people do with it
beat: You come home, and the word you use for it is home.

title: Das Übliche?
desc: Somebody knows what you drink
german: perfect tense with haben; das Übliche, wie immer
swiss: Regulars are recognised but not fussed over; the recognition is the whole event
beat: Lea starts your coffee before you reach the counter.

title: Schönes Wetter heute
desc: Small talk that goes somewhere
german: perfect tense on ordinary verbs; question tags; findest du nicht
swiss: Weather is the opening move, not the conversation, and knowing when to leave it is the skill
beat: Four sentences about rain turn into twenty minutes about something else.

title: Woher kommst du?
desc: The question you will answer a thousand times
german: woher, wohin, seit wann; countries and nationalities
swiss: Asked without edge here, and answered with the town rather than the country
beat: You give your country and get asked which part.

title: Was machst du?
desc: Work, and what it is allowed to mean
german: jobs and workplaces; dative with helfen, arbeiten bei
swiss: Swiss apprenticeships, and why what you trained as matters more than where you studied
beat: Nobody asks what you earn and you notice the absence.

title: Komm essen
desc: An invitation with no date attached
german: imperatives; kommen, bringen, mitbringen
swiss: An invitation that is real comes with a time; one that does not is still worth having
beat: Nuno means it, and proves it by naming a Thursday.

title: In der Küche
desc: A kitchen with four languages in it
german: dative for people; ihm, ihr, uns; food and cooking
swiss: Restaurant kitchens in Luzern are where the country's other half actually talks
beat: Everybody speaks German to you and something else to each other.

title: Timo
desc: Somebody your own age from somewhere near
german: perfect tense in conversation; wir haben, ich bin gegangen
swiss: Nidwalden is fifteen minutes away and considers itself a different country
beat: He says he is from Stans as though that explains something, and later it does.

title: Der Apéro
desc: Drinks that are not dinner and not nothing
german: offering and accepting; möchtest du, ich nehme
swiss: The apéro is its own event with its own rules and its own end time
beat: You arrive hungry and learn that was the mistake.

title: Sie oder du
desc: The most important word you have to choose
german: Sie and du in practice; duzen, siezen; wollen wir
swiss: The switch to du is offered by the older or senior person and it is a small ceremony
beat: Frau Amrein offers you du and you get it wrong twice in one sentence.

title: Wir sollten mal
desc: An invitation that may not be one
german: mal as a softener; sollten, könnten; vague future
swiss: Swiss plans are made in calendars, so a plan with no date is a kindness, not a commitment
beat: You wait three weeks for a message that was never coming.

title: Ja, gern
desc: Saying yes properly
german: accepting; gern, sehr gern, klar; word order in replies
swiss: Enthusiasm is expressed quietly, and gern does most of the work
beat: You say yes to something you do not understand and it turns out fine.

title: Der Verein
desc: You have to join something
german: das Mitglied, der Beitrag, die Probe; joining verbs
swiss: Switzerland runs on Vereine, and belonging to one is how adults make friends here
beat: Timo signs you up for something before asking you.

title: Zieh das an
desc: Fasnacht, from inside a costume
german: clothing; anziehen, ausziehen; imperatives with separable verbs
swiss: You do not watch Fasnacht twice; the second year somebody hands you a costume
beat: You are dressed as something you cannot name and it is four in the afternoon.

title: Raclette
desc: The door opens inward
german: dative in the home; setz dich, gib mir; food at a table
swiss: Being asked into a Swiss home is a real threshold, and raclette is a winter table you sit at for hours
beat: Frau Amrein invites you in, and you are there until eleven.

title: Ihr Mann
desc: Photographs on a sideboard
german: talking about the past; war, hatte; perfect tense on a life
swiss: How the older generation of Luzern talks about the dead, which is plainly and often
beat: She tells you about him for an hour and does not cry once.

title: Früher
desc: Your own past, in a new language
german: perfect tense in narrative; als Kind, damals, vor zehn Jahren
swiss: Being asked about your life and finding you can only tell it simply
beat: You describe your childhood in ninety words and it sounds truer than usual.

title: Herzlichen Glückwunsch
desc: A birthday, done the local way
german: congratulating; wishes and toasts; dative for the person
swiss: You bring your own cake to your own birthday, and you buy the round
beat: You turn up empty handed to your own party.

title: Fünf Minuten zu früh
desc: Being on time is being early
german: time expressions; pünktlich, rechtzeitig, zu spät
swiss: Five minutes early is on time, on time is late, and late needs a message
beat: You send a message saying you are four minutes behind and it is the right call.

title: Das Spiel
desc: A match, and a crowd to stand in
german: sports vocabulary; gewinnen, verlieren, das Tor
swiss: FC Luzern, and how a small city carries a football club
beat: You shout the wrong thing at the wrong moment and get forgiven.

title: Wanderung
desc: A walk that is not a walk
german: planning; treffen, abmachen; wir gehen am Samstag
swiss: Hiking is a national activity with equipment, timings and a printed plan
beat: You say yes to a walk and are sent a list of what to bring.

title: Spazieren
desc: Sunday, and the whole town outside
german: movement verbs; spazieren, wandern, laufen; along and around
swiss: The Sunday walk is what a country does when everything is shut
beat: You meet four people you know in an hour and that has never happened before.

title: Im Brockenhaus
desc: Buying somebody else's past
german: describing objects; adjectives before nouns, first look
swiss: Brockenhaus culture, and the Swiss habit of keeping things until they are worth keeping
beat: Lea talks you out of a lamp and into a better one.

title: Ich habe das falsch verstanden
desc: A misunderstanding, and repairing it
german: clarifying; ich dachte, ich habe gemeint, entschuldigung
swiss: Directness here is not rudeness, and taking it as rudeness is the actual mistake
beat: You take something as an insult for two days before asking.

title: Herr Zemp sagt etwas
desc: The Hauswart thaws by one degree
german: receiving a compliment; small praise; das haben Sie gut gemacht
swiss: Swiss praise is short, rare, and means exactly what it says
beat: He tells you your bicycle is parked correctly and it makes your week.

title: Die Gruppe
desc: Your phone starts making noise
german: written German; short messages; abbreviations people actually use
swiss: How plans really get made, and what a thumbs up commits you to
beat: You are added to a group chat and understand roughly a third of it.

title: Am Samstag?
desc: You have people now
german: review of perfect tense and dative; making arrangements
swiss: The point at which a city stops being somewhere you are and starts being where you live
beat: Three separate people ask what you are doing on Saturday.

title: Das Halbtax
desc: The card everybody has
german: separable verbs: einsteigen, aussteigen, umsteigen; half price
swiss: The Halbtax halves every fare in the country and almost everyone owns one
beat: You work out it pays for itself in six weeks.

title: Die App
desc: A timetable that is never wrong
german: reading times and platforms; abfahren, ankommen; von, nach, ab
swiss: The whole network is timed to connect, and the connections are the point
beat: You plan a journey with three changes and every one of them works.

title: Der Anschluss ist weg
desc: The one time it does not work
german: complaining mildly; verpassen, warten, der nächste
swiss: A missed connection is announced, apologised for, and fixed, which is somehow worse
beat: You miss a train by forty seconds and nobody else seems upset.

title: Das Schiff
desc: The lake has a timetable too
german: two-way prepositions with movement; auf den See, auf dem See
swiss: Lake boats are public transport, not tourism, and the paddle steamers still run
beat: You take a boat because it is faster, which you did not expect.

title: Stansstad
desc: A village where the lake ends
german: in, an, auf with dative; describing where things are
swiss: Nidwalden across the water, and how quickly Luzern stops being Luzern
beat: You get off at the wrong stop and it turns out better.

title: Stans
desc: Timo's town, and its dead hero
german: talking about places; es gibt; historical past in outline
swiss: Winkelried, the Dorfplatz, and a canton of forty thousand people with its own everything
beat: He shows you a statue and expects you to have heard of the man.

title: Das Stanserhorn
desc: A cable car with no roof
german: hinauf, hinunter, oben, unten; separable verbs of motion
swiss: The CabriO is the only double decker cable car with an open top deck
beat: You stand on the roof of a moving cable car and cannot speak.

title: Kriens
desc: The suburb at the foot of the mountain
german: neighbourhoods; wohnen in, arbeiten bei; two-way prepositions settled
swiss: Kriens is where Pilatus starts and where a lot of Luzern actually lives
beat: You realise the mountain you have been looking at has a bus stop.

title: Auf den Pilatus
desc: The steepest railway in the world
german: steigen, fahren, dauern; how long something takes
swiss: The Goldene Rundfahrt: boat to Alpnachstad, cogwheel up, cable car down to Kriens
beat: The train goes up at an angle you would not have believed.

title: Oben
desc: Somebody else is on the summit
german: introductions again, now easy; wem gehört, wer ist das
swiss: Mountain top manners, and the strange formality of greeting strangers on a path
beat: Timo introduces you to Selina and the weather is doing something behind her.

title: Mit der Gondel runter
desc: Twenty minutes and no hurry
german: conversation in motion; small questions; runter, rüber, rein
swiss: Pilatus and its dragons, and which legends the locals actually repeat
beat: You are in a cable car with somebody you have just met and neither of you looks out.

title: Der letzte Zug
desc: The country closes at midnight
german: times and deadlines; verpassen, erwischen, schaffen
swiss: The last train home is a real boundary and everybody knows theirs
beat: You run for it, get it, and wish you had not.

title: Die gelben Schilder
desc: Signs that tell you the time, not the distance
german: reading signs; die Stunde, die Minute; nach, Richtung
swiss: Swiss hiking signs give walking time rather than kilometres, and they are accurate
beat: You take fifteen minutes longer than the sign and are quietly annoyed.

title: Ein Tag in Zürich
desc: The big city, an hour away
german: comparatives; grösser, teurer, schneller als
swiss: What Luzern thinks of Zurich, and how quickly you inherit the opinion
beat: You come back the same evening and are glad to.

title: Die Rigi
desc: The other mountain
german: choosing between options; lieber, am liebsten
swiss: Rigi is the queen of the mountains and the older railway, and people take sides
beat: You admit you preferred Pilatus and start an argument.

title: Das Wetter kippt
desc: Weather that changes its mind
german: weather in detail; der Nebel, der Wind, plötzlich
swiss: Mountain weather, the Nebelmeer, and why the valley can be grey while the top is not
beat: You climb out of the fog into sunlight and understand a word you had only read.

title: Verlaufen
desc: Lost, and having to ask
german: asking for help; sich verlaufen; können Sie mir sagen
swiss: Being lost here is safe, marked, and mildly embarrassing, which is a luxury
beat: A woman with two dogs walks you back to the path.

title: Eine Nachricht
desc: Your phone lights up
german: written German again; reading tone; hast du am Samstag Zeit
swiss: How a Swiss person asks you out, which is to say barely
beat: Selina asks what you are doing on Saturday and you read it eleven times.

title: Nur wir zwei
desc: The first time without anybody else
german: conversation without a safety net; question forms under nerves
swiss: First meetings happen in daylight and involve walking
beat: You talk for four hours and cannot remember any of it afterwards.

title: Der Reuss entlang
desc: A river through the middle of a town
german: entlang, durch, über; describing a route you walked
swiss: The Reuss, the weir, and the wooden bridges that cross it
beat: You walk the same half kilometre three times without noticing.

title: Zu lange geredet
desc: Missing something on purpose
german: consequences; deshalb, darum; simple cause and effect
swiss: What the last train means when you would rather not catch it
beat: You both watch it leave and neither of you mentions it.

title: Ich mag dich
desc: Saying a small thing that is not small
german: mögen, gern haben, and the distance between them
swiss: Understatement in affection, and why the Swiss version sounds cooler than it is
beat: You say it badly and it lands anyway.

title: Was sie macht
desc: A whole person you know nothing about
german: listening; asking follow up questions; und dann, und danach
swiss: Careers here are long and vertical, and people describe them by the training
beat: She explains her job twice before you follow it.

title: Ihre Wohnung
desc: Somebody else's rooms
german: describing interiors; adjective endings begin properly
swiss: What a Swiss flat says about a person, and the plants on every windowsill
beat: You notice she owns forty books and all of them have been read.

title: Der erste Streit
desc: Something small, badly handled
german: disagreeing; das stimmt nicht, so habe ich das nicht gemeint
swiss: How an argument sounds here: quiet, specific, and much more frightening for it
beat: Nobody raises their voice and you would honestly prefer it if they did.

title: Es tut mir leid
desc: Apologising when you have the words for it
german: apology; es tut mir leid, entschuldige, ich war im Unrecht
swiss: Apologies are expected to be specific; a general sorry reads as evasion
beat: You apologise for the wrong thing first and have to start again.

title: Schatz
desc: Words you only use on one person
german: terms of affection; diminutives; du and only du
swiss: Swiss endearments, and how sparingly they are used in public
beat: She calls you something and you have to ask what it means.

title: Nuno weiss es
desc: Telling a friend
german: reported speech, simply; er hat gesagt, dass
swiss: Being teased by a friend as a form of approval
beat: He knew a week before you told him.

title: Frau Amrein hat es gemerkt
desc: The neighbour noticed first
german: perfect tense, gently interrogative; seit wann
swiss: An older neighbour's interest is surveillance and affection at once
beat: She asks a question that proves she has been counting.

title: Sonntagessen in Kriens
desc: Lunch with the parents
german: formal register again; Sie with people you will know for years
swiss: Sunday lunch, the good plates, and an afternoon that lasts until five
beat: You are early, which is correct, and nobody is ready.

title: Ihr Vater sagt wenig
desc: A man who does not fill silences
german: short answers; understanding by inference; question and pause
swiss: Central Swiss reserve, and why a long silence is not disapproval
beat: He asks you two questions in three hours and both of them matter.

title: Ihre Mutter fragt alles
desc: A woman who fills all of them
german: answering personal questions; deflecting politely
swiss: What a Swiss mother is allowed to ask a stranger at a table
beat: You are asked about your pension and you are thirty one.

title: Geprüft
desc: Being assessed without being told
german: indirect language; hedging; eigentlich, eher, vielleicht
swiss: Approval here arrives late, quietly, and to somebody else first
beat: You find out three weeks later that it went well.

title: Ihr Bruder
desc: Somebody who has decided about you already
german: disagreement between equals; das sehe ich anders
swiss: Sibling loyalty, and the test that is not really about you
beat: He is rude once, and she does not defend you, and that is correct.

title: Weihnachten
desc: Christmas with somebody else's family
german: holiday vocabulary; wishes; giving and receiving
swiss: Swiss Christmas is on the twenty fourth, in the evening, and quieter than you expect
beat: You buy presents for nine people and get it roughly right.

title: Silvester
desc: The year turns over
german: future with the present tense; nächstes Jahr, ab Januar
swiss: Fireworks over the lake, and the Swiss habit of making no resolutions out loud
beat: Somebody asks what you want from the year and you answer honestly.

title: Eifersucht
desc: A feeling with no good version
german: emotional vocabulary; eifersüchtig, verletzt, unsicher
swiss: Talking about feelings in a culture that would rather not
beat: You say the thing you have been carrying for a fortnight.

title: Eine schlechte Woche
desc: Nothing wrong, everything heavy
german: describing mood; es geht so, nicht so gut, mies
swiss: How much is contained in a Swiss it is going alright
beat: You answer wie gehts honestly for the first time.

title: Über Geld reden
desc: The conversation nobody wants
german: money and obligation; teilen, schulden, sich leisten
swiss: Money is discussed between couples in detail and almost nowhere else
beat: You split something down to the franc and neither of you finds it strange.

title: Bleibst du?
desc: A question with a country in it
german: conditional beginnings; wenn, dann; plans that are not plans
swiss: What staying actually requires, in permits and in years
beat: She asks in the middle of something else, which is how the big ones arrive.

title: Die Bewilligung
desc: Your life on a piece of plastic
german: bureaucratic vocabulary; verlängern, beantragen, gültig bis
swiss: B and C permits, the years they take, and how a date on a card shapes a decision
beat: You look at an expiry date and feel it in your stomach.

title: Ihre alten Freunde
desc: People who knew her before you
german: group conversation; keeping up; entering a joke halfway
swiss: Swiss friendships formed at fourteen and kept for thirty years
beat: Six people talk about a holiday in 2011 and you laugh in the right places.

title: Mein Deutsch ist heute schlecht
desc: A bad language day, in front of everyone
german: self correction; ich meine, also, wie sagt man
swiss: Being spoken slowly to, and how humiliating kindness can be
beat: Somebody switches to English to help and you ask them not to.

title: Ein guter Tag
desc: Nothing happens, at length
german: ordinary description; the plain present; comfortable silence
swiss: An unremarkable Swiss Saturday, which is most of them
beat: You do almost nothing for eleven hours and it is the best day so far.

title: Ihre Grossmutter
desc: Ninety one, and sharper than anyone
german: older speech; formal address; listening for meaning
swiss: What the oldest generation remembers, and the war that did not happen here
beat: She tells you something about the family that Selina has never heard.

title: Krank
desc: Looking after somebody
german: illness; das Fieber, die Grippe; sich hinlegen, sich ausruhen
swiss: Being ill in Switzerland: the Arztzeugnis, and staying home without apology
beat: You cook badly for someone who cannot taste it anyway.

title: Der Streit, der zählt
desc: The argument that is about the real thing
german: conflict at length; subordinate clauses under pressure
swiss: How far you can go here before something breaks, and where the line sits
beat: You both say the true thing at the same time and it is worse.

title: Zwei Tage nichts
desc: Silence, on purpose
german: absence of language; what is not said; short cold messages
swiss: Swiss cooling off, and the assumption that the other person also needs space
beat: You draft nine messages and send none of them.

title: Wieder gut
desc: Repair, which takes longer than the damage
german: reconciling; ich habe nachgedacht; können wir nochmal
swiss: Making up without ceremony, and the meal that stands in for the apology
beat: Neither of you says sorry again and it is over anyway.

title: Zusammenziehen
desc: Two flats, one lease
german: decisions; sollten wir, was meinst du; practical future
swiss: Getting a flat together in a market where nothing is free
beat: You look at eleven flats and get none of them.

title: Zu Hause anrufen
desc: Explaining Switzerland to your own family
german: explaining; translating culture; das ist hier normal
swiss: Trying to describe the Waschküche to people who think you are joking
beat: Your mother asks when you are coming back and you do not answer quickly enough.

title: Später einmal
desc: A future, said out loud
german: future forms; werden; irgendwann, in ein paar Jahren
swiss: How Swiss couples talk about the long term, which is late and carefully
beat: You say a sentence with the word we in it and a year attached.

title: Ihre Tür ist zu
desc: A door that is always open, closed
german: noticing absence; seit gestern, schon zwei Tage
swiss: How a building notices when somebody stops appearing
beat: You knock twice and then go and find Herr Zemp.

title: Im Spital
desc: A hospital, and the words it needs
german: medical vocabulary; die Station, der Arzt, die Untersuchung
swiss: Spital not Krankenhaus; visiting hours, and the flowers everyone brings
beat: You find the ward by asking four people.

title: Besuch
desc: Sitting with somebody
german: gentle conversation; wie fühlst du dich; small talk with weight
swiss: What you take, what you say, and how long you stay
beat: She wants to talk about the weather and you let her.

title: Was der Arzt sagt
desc: Understanding something you do not want to
german: formal explanation; passive constructions; leider
swiss: Swiss directness in medicine, and being told the truth on the first visit
beat: You understand every word and wish you had understood fewer.

title: Sie redet von ihm
desc: Fifty two years, told out of order
german: narrative past; als, während, damals
swiss: A generation that married once and stayed, and what widowhood looked like
beat: She tells you how they met and you have heard it before and say nothing.

title: Sie bittet dich um etwas
desc: A favour, from somebody who does not ask
german: requests; könntest du, würdest du; Konjunktiv II arrives
swiss: How much it costs a Swiss person of that generation to ask for anything
beat: It takes her four minutes to ask for something that takes you ten.

title: Sie ist gestorben
desc: Three words, and then nothing
german: the vocabulary of death; sterben, gestorben, tot
swiss: How the news travels in a building, and who tells whom
beat: You are at work when your phone buzzes.

title: Herr Zemp klopft
desc: The Hauswart at your door
german: receiving bad news; short exchanges; ich weiss
swiss: Swiss men of sixty and what they do with their hands when they cannot speak
beat: He stands in your doorway for a long time and then says one sentence.

title: Herzliches Beileid
desc: The words people actually use
german: condolence; herzliches Beileid, mein Beileid; what not to say
swiss: Fixed condolence phrases exist so nobody has to invent one
beat: You say it eleven times in one afternoon and mean it every time.

title: Die Abdankung
desc: A funeral, in a church you have walked past
german: ceremony vocabulary; die Trauerfeier, der Pfarrer, das Grab
swiss: The Abdankung, the order of service, and how short a Swiss funeral is
beat: Four hundred people come and you know nine of them.

title: Die Todesanzeige
desc: Her name in the newspaper
german: reading formal text; formulaic language; in stiller Trauer
swiss: Death notices in the local paper, read daily by everybody over sixty
beat: You read the list of names underneath and yours is not there, and it should not be.

title: Die Wohnung wird geräumt
desc: Fifty years, into a van
german: passive voice; wird geräumt, wurde verkauft
swiss: How fast a Swiss flat is emptied and re let, and why it has to be
beat: You carry a chair down three flights and have to stop halfway.

title: Vreni
desc: A sister you did not know existed
german: meeting under bad circumstances; formal to informal in one hour
swiss: Siblings who live twenty minutes apart and saw each other twice a year
beat: She has the same voice and it is very hard to look at her.

title: Sie hat dir etwas hinterlassen
desc: Something small, chosen on purpose
german: inheritance and intent; hinterlassen, vermachen, für dich
swiss: What gets left to a neighbour, and what that means here
beat: It is worth nothing and you will keep it for the rest of your life.

title: Ein ganz normaler Dienstag
desc: Grief on a day with nothing in it
german: describing states; plötzlich, einfach so, mitten am Tag
swiss: How Switzerland expects you to be back at work, and mostly is right
beat: You are fine until you see soup in a supermarket.

title: Anders trauern
desc: Two people, two speeds
german: talking about feeling; ich brauche, lass mich, ich kann nicht
swiss: Grief that is not shared equally, and the resentment that grows in the gap
beat: She is ready to talk about it on the day you are not.

title: Aus Trauer gestritten
desc: A fight about something else entirely
german: argument with subtext; darum geht es nicht
swiss: Anger with nowhere to go, and the nearest available target
beat: You shout about the dishwasher for twenty minutes.

title: Beat holt dich raus
desc: Somebody makes you leave the flat
german: invitations that are not requests; komm jetzt, du kommst mit
swiss: The Verein as a safety net, and how Swiss men look after each other without saying so
beat: He does not ask how you are, which is exactly right.

title: Woher kommst du wirklich?
desc: A question asked of somebody born here
german: identity and belonging; eigentlich, wirklich, ursprünglich
swiss: Second generation Switzerland, the red passport, and the question that never stops
beat: Fatlum has answered it four thousand times and answers it again.

title: Es reicht nicht
desc: Money, and running out of it
german: finance under strain; die Miete, das Konto, die Schulden
swiss: How expensive Switzerland is, and how invisible poverty is here
beat: You do arithmetic at a kitchen table at one in the morning.

title: Probleme bei der Arbeit
desc: Something going wrong at work
german: workplace conflict; formal complaint; ich möchte etwas ansprechen
swiss: Swiss workplace hierarchy, and the meeting you have to ask for
beat: You rehearse four sentences and use one of them.

title: Nein sagen
desc: Refusing somebody you love
german: refusal; leider nein, das geht nicht, ich kann nicht
swiss: Saying no clearly, and why hedging is read as dishonest here
beat: You say no without an excuse and the sky does not fall.

title: Sie trennen sich
desc: Friends, coming apart
german: talking about other people; sich trennen, die Scheidung
swiss: Taking sides, and the Swiss preference for not
beat: Both of them tell you their version and you believe both.

title: Selber krank
desc: Your own body, letting you down
german: symptoms and appointments; der Termin, die Überweisung
swiss: Navigating the system as a foreigner, and what the insurance actually covers
beat: You describe a pain in a language you did not learn for this.

title: Um Hilfe bitten
desc: Asking, which you have avoided
german: asking properly; Konjunktiv II fully; ich hätte eine Bitte
swiss: How readily help is given here once it is actually requested
beat: Four people say yes immediately and you feel stupid for waiting.

title: Es wird leichter
desc: Not better, lighter
german: reflection; langsam, mit der Zeit, allmählich
swiss: A year of Swiss seasons, and what the first warm day does to a town
beat: You laugh at something in March and catch yourself doing it.

title: Halt
desc: The word for that is simply how it is
german: halt as a particle; resignation, acceptance, closing a topic
swiss: The most Swiss word there is, and the shrug built into it
beat: You use it correctly by accident and somebody looks at you.

title: Eben
desc: Agreeing with something you already thought
german: eben; confirming, concluding, saying I told you so gently
swiss: Agreement without enthusiasm, which is the local default
beat: An entire conversation is conducted in one syllable.

title: Doch
desc: Contradicting a negative
german: doch as an answer and as a particle; insisting politely
swiss: A word English has no version of, and how much work it does
beat: You finally use doch as an answer and it feels like a door opening.

title: Mach mal
desc: Softening everything
german: mal as a softener; imperatives that are not orders
swiss: How a direct instruction is made bearable in three letters
beat: You notice that everything anybody asks of you has a mal in it.

title: Nicht schlecht
desc: The highest praise available
german: understatement; nicht schlecht, ganz gut, geht so
swiss: Swiss praise, calibrated downward, and how to hear it correctly
beat: Your cooking is called not bad and Selina explains what happened.

title: Sie nehmen dich auf den Arm
desc: Being teased on purpose
german: idiom; recognising a joke; the flat delivery that hides one
swiss: Teasing as inclusion, and the flat face it is delivered with
beat: You believe something ridiculous for four minutes.

title: Zurückgeben
desc: Teasing back
german: wit in a second language; timing; short comebacks
swiss: Being allowed to give it back is the moment you are actually in
beat: You land one, and the table goes quiet and then does not.

title: Trockener Humor
desc: Jokes with no signal on them
german: deadpan; irony markers, or the lack of them
swiss: Central Swiss humour, which is dry to the point of invisibility
beat: Herr Zemp makes a joke and it takes you until evening.

title: Reklamieren
desc: Complaining as a social form
german: formal complaint; das kann ja nicht sein; polite outrage
swiss: Complaining about trains, prices and Zurich as a shared national pastime
beat: You complain about a four minute delay and mean it.

title: Die Guggenmusik
desc: A brass band playing wrong on purpose
german: music vocabulary; die Probe, der Marsch, das Instrument
swiss: Guggenmusik, and why the dissonance is the entire point
beat: Beat hands you an instrument and does not explain it.

title: Falsch spielen
desc: Being bad at something in public
german: self deprecation; ich kann das nicht, ich übe noch
swiss: How much room there is here for being an enthusiastic amateur
beat: You play badly in front of two hundred people and nobody minds.

title: Die Grinde
desc: A mask, and what it lets you do
german: costume and disguise; sich verkleiden, die Maske, das Kostüm
swiss: The Grinde, the anonymity it gives, and the licence that comes with it
beat: Behind a mask your German is suddenly fluent.

title: Der Urknall
desc: Five in the morning on Kapellplatz
german: describing chaos; überall, plötzlich, tausend
swiss: Schmutziger Donnerstag begins at five with the Urknall, in the dark, in February
beat: You are in a crowd in the dark and the whole city goes off at once.

title: Räppli
desc: Confetti in everything for a month
german: quantity; voll, überall, immer noch
swiss: Räppli not Konfetti, and how long it stays in your coat pockets
beat: You find some in a jacket in July.

title: Drei Tage
desc: Sleep is not part of it
german: endurance; müde, kaputt, weiter; time running together
swiss: What the city does for six days and what it looks like on the seventh
beat: You lose track of which day it is and so has everyone else.

title: Aschermittwoch
desc: It stops, completely
german: endings; vorbei, fertig, Schluss
swiss: How abruptly Fasnacht ends, and the town sweeping up by nine in the morning
beat: By breakfast there is no evidence any of it happened.

title: Ironie, aber freundlich
desc: Sarcasm that is not unkind
german: tone; the line between teasing and rudeness
swiss: Where the line sits here, and how badly a foreigner usually places it
beat: You go slightly too far and are told, kindly, where the edge was.

title: Fluchen, ein bisschen
desc: Swearing, at the local strength
german: mild expletives; what is acceptable and where
swiss: Swiss swearing, which is agricultural, regional, and much milder than German
beat: You use a German swear word and the temperature drops.

title: Die Deutschen
desc: The neighbours, discussed
german: opinions held lightly; comparison; typisch
swiss: How the Swiss talk about Germans, and the accent that gives a German away instantly
beat: You are told you sound German and it is not a compliment.

title: Zürich
desc: The other city, discussed
german: rivalry; grösser, schneller, kälter; expressing preference
swiss: What a Luzerner thinks of Zurich, and the thirty five minutes between them
beat: You defend Zurich once and never again.

title: Der Röstigraben
desc: A country with a line down it
german: regional vocabulary; the French side; borrowed words
swiss: The Röstigraben, the four languages, and how differently the country votes across it
beat: You go to Fribourg for a weekend and half the words change.

title: Abstimmen
desc: Voting, four times a year
german: political vocabulary; die Initiative, die Abstimmung, dagegen, dafür
swiss: Direct democracy, the envelope on the kitchen table, and turnout of about forty five percent
beat: You cannot vote, and somebody asks your opinion anyway.

title: Eine Meinung, locker gehalten
desc: Having a view without insisting on it
german: hedged opinion; ich finde eigentlich, mir scheint
swiss: Consensus culture, and why a strong opinion is stated weakly here
beat: You state something flatly and watch the table adjust.

title: Du tönst schon fast
desc: Somebody says you sound like one of them
german: receiving praise; abwehren; ach was, übertreib nicht
swiss: How rarely this is said, and why it is not said to your face twice
beat: Nuno says it, which means more than if a Swiss person had.

title: Jahre später
desc: Time, measured backwards
german: long time spans; seit, vor, inzwischen; the pluperfect
swiss: What changes in a Swiss town in five years, which is almost nothing and everything
beat: You catch yourself giving directions to somebody.

title: Ohne nachzudenken
desc: Words you use without choosing them
german: idiom in the wild; fixed expressions; automatic speech
swiss: The point at which the language stops being a task
beat: You say a whole paragraph and only afterwards notice which language it was in.

title: Wortspiele
desc: Jokes that only work in German
german: wordplay; compound humour; puns on separable verbs
swiss: Swiss humour that cannot survive translation, and the pleasure of that
beat: You make one, deliberately, and it works.

title: Unser Witz
desc: A joke with a history
german: shared reference; in jokes; short callbacks
swiss: Friendships measured in running jokes rather than in conversations
beat: Timo says four words and you both laugh for a long time.

title: Bei den Odermatts
desc: The house where you now take your shoes off
german: familiarity in formal settings; du with people who were Sie
swiss: How long it takes to become family here, and what it looks like when you have
beat: Her father asks your opinion about something that matters to him.

title: Vreni und du
desc: Her sister, every second Sunday
german: habitual past; immer, jeden Sonntag, damals
swiss: Inherited relationships, and the obligations nobody names
beat: You have been going for three years and neither of you has ever mentioned why.

title: Eine Hochzeit
desc: A day with speeches in it
german: formal register; toasts; speaking in front of people
swiss: A Swiss wedding, the civil ceremony first, and how long the speeches run
beat: You are asked to say something and you say it in German.

title: Anna
desc: Somebody newer than you
german: simplifying your own speech; explaining without condescending
swiss: Recognising the specific look of somebody three weeks into Switzerland
beat: She asks you where the rubbish goes and you talk for forty minutes.

title: Die Waschküche erklären
desc: The rota, explained to a foreigner
german: instructions; imperatives; du musst, du darfst nicht
swiss: Handing on the rules that nearly broke you
beat: You hear yourself defending the rota and stop mid sentence.

title: Wohin kommt der Karton
desc: Rubbish, explained again
german: repetition as teaching; patience; nochmal, ganz einfach
swiss: How obvious it all is once, and how impossible it is at first
beat: You draw her a diagram.

title: Warum Grüezi
desc: The first word, explained last
german: metalanguage; talking about language; man sagt, das heisst
swiss: Why the greeting matters, said by somebody who once did not know
beat: You explain it better than anybody ever explained it to you.

title: Warum lädt mich niemand ein?
desc: The question everybody asks eventually
german: consolation; das kommt noch, das dauert; encouragement
swiss: Swiss friendship on its real timescale, which is years and not weeks
beat: You tell her the truth, which is that it takes about two years.

title: Von Frau Amrein erzählen
desc: Telling somebody about the dead
german: narrative past at length; character description
swiss: Keeping somebody present by describing them accurately
beat: You tell Anna about the soup and about the recycling and about the door.

title: Ins Brockenhaus
desc: Furnishing another empty flat
german: advice; an dessen Stelle würde ich; Konjunktiv II casually
swiss: The same warehouse, the same lamps, a different person deciding
beat: You talk her out of a lamp.

title: Sie lernt alle kennen
desc: Introducing somebody to your people
german: introductions from the inside; das ist, kennst du schon
swiss: Bringing somebody into a circle, and the responsibility of it
beat: Nuno takes to her immediately and it is briefly annoying.

title: Das Heft
desc: A notebook, handed over
german: handing on knowledge; das brauchst du, das hilft
swiss: The notes you took in your first year and never threw away
beat: You give her the notebook you kept and half of it is wrong.

title: Nichts war schwierig
desc: A day with no difficulty in it
german: fluent ordinary speech; the whole grammar, unremarked
swiss: An unremarkable day, which is the entire achievement
beat: You get to the evening before realising nothing was hard.

title: Niemand wechselt ins Englische
desc: They stop switching
german: the full range, used normally; no scaffolding left
swiss: The moment Switzerland stops handling you, which nobody announces
beat: You are in a conversation with four people and not one of them changes language for you.
